newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-NAB no show at Advance merger hearing.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-NAB no show at Advance merger hearing.

text.p: The Supreme Court of New South Wales was told on Monday that National Australia Bank Ltd (NAB) would not appear at a hearing to approve the merger between Advance Bank Australia Ltd and St George Bank Ltd.
Justice Kim Santow asked the court if NAB would be appearing at the hearing into the merger of the two Sydney-based banks.
A legal representatives for Advance said that as far as he was aware NAB would not be making an appearance at the hearing.
NAB has been seen as a potential blocker of the merger as it has built up stakes in both St George and Advance.
Representatives for the Australian Securities Commission (ASC) told the court that it would make a submission to the hearing, but it would not oppose the scheme.
The hearing was adjourned by Justice Sandow until midday so that he could read submissions from Advance and the ASC.
Earlier the two banks set their merger terms.

Under the proposal Advance Bank ordinary shareholders would receive 0.625 of a new St George Bank ordinary share, A$2.10 in cash from St George and a 20 cent per share special dividend for each Advance Bank share as payment for the planned merger of the two banks.
The terms set were based on the weighted average St George Bank share price, ex-final dividend, in the 20 business days up to January 3, of A$7.90.

National Australia Bank Ltd, which holds 6.8 percent of St George, has also said it owns three percent of Advance. NAB, which is seen as interested in buying regional banks, has not said whether it opposes the merger.
